prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The map separates the nearby road surface from the darker, more distant trees, buildings, and sky, showing an open roadway extending forward with vegetation and structures along both sides. A person appears near the right edge of frame 1 and near the center-right of frame 2, roughly 2–4 m away; in frame 4 a person occupies much more of the right side and appears about 1–2 m away, while no person is clearly represented in frames 3 or 5. The person is upright, extends above the road plane, and is within possible arm’s reach only in frame 4; the changing image position and scale support relative approach or camera turning, but do not distinguish those motions reliably. This map makes foreground distance ordering and dark silhouettes clearer than RGB, but its metre estimates are uncertain because the depth is monocular, distant regions collapse into similar dark values, object boundaries are soft, and the person is partly cut off at frame edges.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no usable object instances, class labels, boundaries, or spatial relationships. It does not identify the road, lamps, trees, buildings, or the person visible in the RGB and depth strips, and therefore cannot support distance, facing direction, reach, or occlusion estimates. The missing masks are especially unreliable where a person appears near the right edge in frames 1–2 and much larger on the right in frame 4. Consequently, this map shows nothing spatial that is unavailable in RGB and appears to represent detector failure or absent segmentation output.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, with no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons. It therefore provides no evidence about body orientation, head or gaze direction, limb positions, hand locations, interpersonal spacing, or whether anyone is within another person’s reach. In particular, it fails to represent the person visible in frames 1–2 and the larger, partly edge-cropped person in frame 4, so turning, approach, and self-occlusion cannot be tracked from this map. The map adds no spatial information beyond RGB and is unreliable here because no pose detections are present.
